name: Tregâmi
confidence_why: The only statement on Tregâmi accent is Strand's survey remark (2010; repeated in his 2007-2016 transcription notes) that stress 'apparently' falls on the last syllable of the stem, which Strand himself marks with a question mark and which rests on no first-hand Tregâmi data, while Grjunberg 1999 says the scant material allows no linguistic characterization and Morgenstierne 1952, the one primary description, is not accessible.

catalog_quote: [Iranica, 'Phonology'] Accent is indicated by ' before a vowel in K. and V., where it is phonemic. In the remaining groups (including Tr.?) accent apparently falls automatically on the last syllable of a word's stem. [Iranica, item 5] Tregâmi (abbr. “Tr.”, native name unrecorded) is spoken in the three villages of Gambir, Kaṭâr, and Devoz in the Tregâm Valley off the lower Pech. ... A., Kal., and Tr. form a Southern Nurestâni cluster ['Position and Representation of Accent'] Accent is indicated by ʹ before a vowel in K. and V., the two languages in which accentual position is distinctive. ... In the remaining languages (including Tr.?) accent falls automatically on a word's final syllable (excluding inflectional or enclitic suffixes) and is not written. ['Sources and Reliability'] Data from K.km, K.ktv, Kal.n, Kal.v, A.s, and V.ṣupu were collected in the field by this author (Strand). Data from other dialects are from Morgentierne (1929a, 1934a, 1949, 1952, 1954, and unpublished) ... Morgenstierne's data are largely pre-phonemic

new_statements.rule_in_words: Per Strand's survey generalization for the Southern Nuristani group, stress is non-contrastive and falls automatically on the last syllable of the word stem, not counting inflectional or enclitic suffixes; Strand marks Tregami with an explicit question mark, i.e. he had no first-hand data and extends the Kalasha-ala/Ashkun pattern to it.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Tregami; the whole statement is hedged ('apparently', 'Tr.?'). Note that the only primary source, Morgenstierne 1952 pp. 121-135, contains no tokens 'accent'/'stress'/'syllable' but does use 'falling-rising tone', 'rising tone', 'falling tone' on pp. 124 and 130 (index probes only), so the primary description is of a tonal contrast (apparently from lost voiced aspirates), not stress placement; Edel'man 1999: 99 conversely says tone oppositions are noted only in Dameli.
new_statements.domain_note: Word stem (excludes inflectional/enclitic suffixes); citation-form generalization across languages, no Tregami examples given.
new_statements.identity_note: Tregami = Gambiri (Morgenstierne's name), spoken in Gambir, Katar and Devoz (Tregam valley, Kunar/Nuristan). Morgenstierne 1952's data are labelled 'Gambir' in his word list; Degener 2022 describes the Devozi village dialect. Glottolog has no separate dialect codes. Strand's abbreviation 'Tr.' = Tregâmi.
